text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- A bill on higher education financing proposes that the government will contribute to fees in courses considered to be important that are taught in private universities.

- Portuguese Economy Minister Augusto Mateus and Spanish Industry Minister Josep Pique said in Lisbon yesterday that they favoured EDP-Electricidade de Portugal taking a stake in the privatisation of Spanish utility Endesa, and Endesa taking a stake in EDP. No decisions had been taken.

- UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi has told U.N. Secretary- General Kofi Annan that the members of parliament of the Angolan opposition group would be in Luanda today to take part in a new government of national unity.
- The European Commission has presented a complaint against the Portuguese government because the Agricultural and Health Ministries did not implement European directives in national legislation.
- The Portuguese government will give incentives to farmers and agricultural companies that start operations in Portuguese- speaking countries.
- A future decree-law foresees consultation with the local population when a plan is presented to open a hypermarket in an area of more than 10,000 square metres.

- Export growth rates of about five percent in 1996, below double digit growth of the previous two years, made an insignificant contribution to overall Portuguese economic growth, according to an INE report.
- According to a study by the Economist Intelligence Unit, Portugal has high ratings on its loans.
